card.stem: A triple glazed window with a wooden frame is fitted in the external wall of a dwelling house as shown. The fixed frame of the window is 100 mm × 80 mm. The wall is of timber frame construction with an external concrete block leaf. The internal timber frame is 250 mm × 50 mm and the outer leaf is of 100 mm concrete block construction with an external render finish. A 50 mm service cavity is also provided at the internal surface. card.stem: The sketch shows a row of terraced townhouses built over 100 years ago. A young couple have purchased one of the houses and have decided to refurbish it as their family home.
card.questionText: The owners commissioned a survey of the house which revealed the following: traditional cut roof with natural slates; softwood sliding sash windows with single-glazing; solid external walls of brick construction, uninsulated and with internal lime render. Select any two of the above areas and, using notes and freehand sketches, describe in detail the steps involved in upgrading each area selected in a manner that respects the appearance and character of the original townhouses.

rows.contextNote: Any two of the three printed areas, each notes 10 and sketches 8 = 18. Traditional cut roof with natural slates: remove the slates carefully, clean only their undersides of lime parging, weigh and grade them and refit the heaviest at the eaves; replace decayed rafter ends, wallplate and fascia in the same species and profiles; a vapour-diffuse breathable membrane with counter battens; cast-iron rainwater goods; hygroscopic insulation such as sheep’s wool with woodfibre board, and a thoroughly ventilated roof. Softwood sliding sash windows with single - glazing: repair rather than replace, by a specialist conservation joiner; remove the sashes and glass carefully and record their positions; replace rotten timber in the same species with traditional joints and animal glue; free the pulleys, renew the cords and reuse the counter-balance weights; non-toxic paint; discreet secondary glazing. Solid external walls of brick construction, uninsulated and with internal lime render: never cement mortar; have the lime mortar analysed and matched (NHL strength, sand); rake out by hand to twice the joint width and repoint in stages, protected with hessian; internally, hempcrete or an insulating lime plaster system with a three-coat lime render.

options: Traditional cut roof with natural slates
Softwood sliding sash windows with single - glazing
Solid external walls of brick construction, uninsulated and with internal lime render

card.stem: The external wall of a house built in the 1990s is of 100 mm concrete block construction with a 100 mm partially filled cavity, as shown.
card.questionText:
Calculate the U-value of the wall, given the construction has the following sequence and data: External render thickness 16 mm; Concrete block outer leaf thickness 100 mm; Clear cavity width 50 mm; Polystyrene insulation thickness 50 mm; Concrete block inner leaf thickness 100 mm; Internal plaster thickness 12 mm.
Thermal data of the external wall: Resistance of external surface (R) 0.048 m2 °C/W; Resistivity of external render (r) 2.170 m °C/W; Conductivity of concrete external blockwork (k) 1.440 W/m °C; Resistance of clear cavity (R) 0.170 m2 °C/W; Conductivity of insulation (k) 0.037 W/m °C; Conductivity of concrete internal blockwork (k) 1.440 W/m °C; Resistivity of internal plaster (r) 6.250 m °C/W; Resistance of internal surface (R) 0.122 m2 °C/W.

rows.contextNote: Eight resistances, 3 each, by R = T/k (or R = T × r for render and plaster): external surface 0.048 (given); render 0.016 × 2.170 = 0.035; external blockwork 0.1/1.44 = 0.069; clear cavity 0.170 (given); insulation 0.05/0.037 = 1.351; internal blockwork 0.1/1.44 = 0.069; plaster 0.012 × 6.25 = 0.075; internal surface 0.122 (given). All in m²°C/W.
Total resistance Rt = 1.939 m²°C/W.
U = 1 ÷ Rt = 1 ÷ 1.939 = 0.516 W/m²°C, with units.
